einzeiler: Investigative analyst Leah files discusses corporate fraud, intelligence work, and state…
kurzfassung: Corporate intelligence consultant and former intelligence contractor Leah files joins the show to discuss her background, investigations into nonprofit finances, and government surveillance. She explains how financial follow-the-money techniques uncover hidden realities behind corporate and political organizations. They also examine contentious topics including the tracking capabilities of modern automated license plate readers and foreign influence campaigns.
stichpunkte: Leah files runs a corporate intelligence firm called Black Widow Global, focusing on due diligence, fraud, and hidden financial relationships.
She describes her upbringing in a toxic and abusive household in North Carolina, noting that she has few memories before age fourteen.
During her career as a government contractor, she built cost models for satellites and worked for agencies including the CIA, NGA, and DIA.
She examines the financial disclosures of Turning Point USA, pointing to high vendor payments and heavy reliance on a small number of top donors.
The discussion covers the mechanics of foreign influence campaigns within the United States, specifically referencing Brad Parscale's registered operations.
They explore terms of service anomalies in consumer software, highlighting the jurisdictional requirements of apps like Waze.
The conversation addresses automated license plate reader networks like Flock and the privacy implications revealed by public audit logs.

clips.hook: A client died mysteriously days into an investigation.
clips.text: While performing due diligence on a domestic target for an overseas client, the client died suddenly under suspicious circumstances within days of signing the contract.

clips.hook: A massive surge in funding for a prominent political nonprofit.
clips.text: The organization experienced an extreme revenue increase in a single year, jumping past one hundred million dollars while depending on just a handful of primary financial contributors.

clips.hook: Conference expenses consume a huge portion of nonprofit budgets.
clips.text: Large conventions and events represent the primary operating expense for the organization, even though attendees must pay out of pocket to participate.

clips.hook: The vast majority of license plate reader searches lack valid crime justificatio
clips.text: Public audit records indicate that only a small single-digit percentage of recorded vehicle database lookups are connected to actual criminal cases or warrants.

clips.hook: Surveillance tech investors linked to real-time video tampering tools.
clips.text: Financial backers of automated vehicle tracking hardware also maintain connections to sophisticated software designed to alter live camera footage without leaving forensic traces.

beschreibung:
Leah,
I chose not to release your episode because I personally had serious concerns about the truthfulness of your statements. I take what I put out on my platform seriously for myself and for my listeners. For the sake of transparency, here's the full interview so everyone can watch and draw their own conclusions.

As for my investments, I've intentionally made them public, as you see on my LinkedIn. I invest in Shield AI and Anduril for no other reason than I believe in their ability to develop technology that equips and protects the American warfighter. That's something deeply personal to me that I believe in.
